title: Transceiver design, filters and SDR
blurb: Explain how SSB is made and received, what filter terms mean, and how DDS and software-defined radios work.

G7C01.why: A balanced modulator gives both sidebands. A **filter** removes one, leaving a single sideband.
G7C01.trap: The IF and RF amplifiers only amplify. They do not select a sideband.

G7C02.why: A balanced modulator mixes audio with a carrier, cancels the carrier, and outputs **double-sideband** RF.
G7C02.trap: It makes no FM, and it does not extract audio.

G7C03.why: A transformer **presents the desired impedance** to the transmitter and to the feed line.
G7C03.trap: The aim is to transfer power well, not to minimise it.

G7C04.why: A **product detector** mixes the SSB signal with a carrier in an SSB receiver and recovers the audio.
G7C04.trap: It is not test gear, a multiplier, or an FM filter.

G7C05.why: A DDS gives a **variable output frequency**, set digitally, with the **stability of a crystal** oscillator.
G7C05.trap: A DDS tunes over a wide range and its raw output needs filtering and amplifying.

G7C06.why: A DSP filter is software, so a **wide range of bandwidths and shapes** can be created by changing numbers.
G7C06.trap: DSP does not reduce mixing products, and it is not a VHF-specific advantage.

G7C07.why: **Insertion loss** is the attenuation inside the passband.
G7C07.trap: Ultimate rejection is attenuation outside the passband.

G7C08.why: Gain, noise figure and bandwidth each change how weak a signal can be and still be heard: **all of them**.
G7C08.trap: Each choice is true. None is the only factor.

G7C09.why: The I and Q signals are **90°** apart: one cosine, one sine.
G7C09.trap: At 0° or 180° the two would not be independent.

G7C10.why: Varying I and Q gives any amplitude and phase, so **all types of modulation** can be made by processing.
G7C10.trap: An SDR still needs an ADC. I-Q does not remove that need.

G7C11.why: After the ADC, the SDR does **filtering, detection and modulation** in software.

G7C12.why: Above the **cutoff frequency**, a low-pass filter's output power is less than half the input.
G7C12.trap: Notch is where a notch filter rejects. Rolloff describes steepness, not a frequency.

G7C13.why: **Ultimate rejection** is the most a filter can reject outside its passband.
G7C13.trap: Rolloff is steepness. Insertion loss is attenuation inside the passband.

G7C14.why: Band-pass bandwidth is measured between the **upper and lower half-power** points.
G7C14.trap: Rolloff is steepness, not a frequency. Image and harmonic are unrelated.
